evals.name: review-the-current-diff
evals.setup: A staged diff that drops one error return and wraps another with `fmt.Errorf` using `%v` instead of `%w`. Nothing names a target.

evals.name: broad-target-auto-plan-first
evals.setup: A module of eleven packages. The invocation names no budget and no depth. The user answers the proposal in a following turn with "go ahead, those defaults are fine", so the run continues past the gate in the same session.

evals.name: rule-edit-add-change-remove
evals.setup: `../style/SKILL.md` already carries a receiver-naming rule. The session issues three rule edits in turn.
evals.query: /review add "no naked returns in tests", then /review change "receivers are three letters", then /review remove "the compile-time check rule"

evals.name: learn-from-the-session
evals.setup: A finished session with four corrections. Two are genuinely absent from `../style/SKILL.md`: the user rejected a `time.After` inside a `select` loop because each iteration leaks a timer until it fires, and asked that a string built in a loop use `strings.Builder` rather than `+=`. One repeats a rule the rulebook already carries verbatim — never store a `context.Context` in a struct field. The fourth was a rename specific to this project's domain vocabulary.

evals.name: broad-fix-job-plans-and-pauses
evals.setup: Findings span five packages, one of them large enough to warrant file-level chunks. The user answers each pause with "go ahead" in a following turn, so the run works at least the first two chunks rather than stopping at the plan.

evals.name: learn-finds-nothing-new
evals.setup: A session whose three Go corrections are all already rules in `../style/SKILL.md` — `%w` wrapping, `have`/`want` test naming, and receiver conventions. Nothing new was taught.
